argument_summary: The certification defense should be read narrowly. The admissible record supports launch readiness and a monitored staged rollout: aggregate readiness passed by 2.1 points, rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, and rollout begins at 8% with rollback capability. The same admissible record also shows the enterprise password recovery segment remains below target and exposed, and that the current risk acceptance draft is neither approved nor specific to that exposure. On that record, the defensible position is not that rollout controls alone cure the issue, but that certification is supportable only if treated as caveated and paired with explicit disclosure of the unresolved limitation in the certification/model-card record.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to resolve the audit issue. The admissible basis for limiting escalation is that the release passed aggregate readiness and is designed for monitored, reversible rollout, which can justify a bounded certification posture if the auditor records the unresolved limitation rather than treating the launch as an unqualified pass.
claims_about_policy: The policy cuts against any controls-only argument. It says rollout controls and post-launch monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or approved risk acceptance explains why exposure is acceptable. The admissible evidence shows neither exclusion nor approved risk acceptance. It also says disclosure remains required when the affected segment stays exposed. So the proper policy characterization is caveated certification with mandatory disclosure of the enterprise password recovery limitation, not a clean compliance finding based solely on staged rollout and rollback monitoring.
concessions: The present admissible record does not support a clean claim that rollout controls alone satisfy policy.
The affected enterprise password recovery use case remains exposed in the initial cohort.
The current risk acceptance draft is incomplete because it is unapproved and does not address the specific exposed segment.
The available admissible evidence here does not itself show the final disclosure artifact or approval record.
